title: Evaluating & Choosing LLMs — Choose Along a Frontier, Not One Score
key_insight: Plot the quality-cost-latency frontier and remove choices that are worse on all important dimensions. Apply hard safety or privacy constraints before trading softer goals.
body:
## Choose Along a Frontier, Not One Score

One model is cheaper and faster; another is more accurate. Neither dominates every objective.

Plot the quality-cost-latency frontier and remove choices that are worse on all important dimensions. Apply hard safety or privacy constraints before trading softer goals.

Use online experiments only after offline gates pass. Monitor real task success and rollback signals, because production traffic differs from a frozen test set.
common_mistakes: The biggest model is automatically best for every product.
One public benchmark replaces task-specific testing.
A model-based grader is perfectly objective and never changes.
mini_exercise: Draw “Choose Along a Frontier, Not One Score” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Model families and versions change quickly, so a repeatable evaluation process is more durable than one recommendation.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Choose Along a Frontier, Not One Score,” explain Evaluating & Choosing LLMs without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
